paper_title: OMNIGUARD An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across   Modalities
caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.

model_annotations.German: This plot illustrates the accuracy of various models in detecting harmful prompts under different numbers of few-shot examples, with the x-axis representing the number of few-shot examples and labeled as "Number of Few-Shot Examples" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 5 with integer tick labels, and the y-axis representing accuracy and labeled as "Accuracy" on a linear scale ranging from 50 to 90 with a tick label interval of 10. The plot displays six lines representing different models, including OmniGuard, shown in black with a solid line style and circle markers, which starts at 50% accuracy at 0 few-shot examples and increases to approximately 96.5% at 5 few-shot examples; AegisGuard (P), shown in blue with a solid line style and cross markers, which starts at around 70% and decreases to about 53% across the x-axis range; AegisGuard (D), represented in red with a solid line style and plus sign markers, which begins at approximately 65% and declines to around 50% across the x-axis; LlamaGuard 1, depicted in green with a solid line style and square markers, which remains relatively stable around 50% across the x-axis; LlamaGuard 2, shown in orange with a solid line style and diamond markers, which starts above 87% and slightly increases across the x-axis; and DuoGuard, represented in purple with a solid line style and triangle markers, which begins at 50% and remains relatively constant across the x-axis, with all lines having error bars indicating the standard error of the mean accuracy averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples.
